text: Cost management and optimization — turning capacity units into an actual conversation about spend.

A hopping window recomputes overlapping aggregates, touching each event several times — that's real cost, not just an abstract tradeoff. Long retention on a KQL database costs storage indefinitely, whether or not anyone ever queries it.

A retention policy ages out data past a defined point automatically. Thirty days might be generous for a dashboard, or necessary for compliance — the right number depends on how the data actually gets used.

Knowing the bill was four thousand two hundred dollars tells you almost nothing. Knowing sixty percent of it is one hopping-window tile, and switching it would cut the bill in half — that's actually being cost-aware.
Know why, not just how much. Next up: right-sizing compute — matching capacity to actual need.
